isolation_claim.claim: promoter_calculator pulls sklearn 1.9.1, so it must live in an ISOLATED interpreter or it would move sklearn under the whole test suite
isolation_claim.status: CONSEQUENCE REFUTED, antecedent HOLDS -- measured 2026-10-22; read `evidence` and `antecedent_holds` rather than this one line
isolation_claim.antecedent_holds: a FRESH `uv venv` + `uv pip install promotercalculator` installed scikit-learn 1.9.1, so 'pulls sklearn 1.9.1' is true of an unconstrained resolve; what is refuted is the CONSEQUENCE that installing it in the project env would move sklearn under the suite
isolation_claim.isolation_still_correct_because: `uv.lock` is a frozen reproducibility unit, so `uv add` is unavailable and an imperative `uv pip install` into the project env is silently reverted by the next `uv sync`. The separate venv is near-free and keeps the boundary that tests/test_promcalc_decompose.py now enforces.
isolation_claim.evidence: the distribution is `promotercalculator` 1.2.4 -- a py3-none-any PURE-PYTHON wheel, requires_python=None, with UNPINNED deps (biopython, numpy, scikit-learn, scipy). `uv pip install --dry-run promotercalculator` resolved 7 packages and would install exactly ONE (promotercalculator), leaving sklearn 1.8.0 untouched. There is no hard pin to 1.9.1 anywhere in its metadata; 1.9.1 is simply what an unconstrained resolver picks when it takes the latest.
isolation_claim.not_measured_by_this_probe: this probe issues NO subprocess by contract, so it cannot run that resolution itself. The dry-run was performed separately and its result is RECORDED here, not re-derived at call time. Re-run it if the lockfile or the dep set changes.
isolation_claim.install_name_differs_from_import_name: import `promoter_calculator`, but `pip install promoter_calculator` 404s -- the distribution on PyPI is `promotercalculator` (Salis Lab, Barrick Lab fork).
